newsitem.title: USA: Major oil company executives preach moderation.
newsitem.headline: Major oil company executives preach moderation.

text.p: Flush with record earnings fueled by strong crude oil prices, executives of several major oil companies preached moderation to avoid another era of over- investment by the industry.

After setting capital budgets and pegging business plans to crude oil prices in the $18 a barrel range last year, the major U.S. oil companies posted solid earnings as crude prices floated above $22 a barrel by the year's end.

"Along with the euphoria comes a very human urge to relax our discipline in relation to cost and expense," Texaco Inc Chairman Peter Bijur said at Canbridge Energy Research Associates annual energy forum running through Wednesday.
"We should also ask ourselves whether the current period of prosperity will lead to another cycle of over-investment followed by a downturn," said H.L. Fuller, Amoco Corp chairman.

Fuller cautioned that oil companies angling to enter the global gas and independent power markets need to consider how the investments fit into an overall corporate strategy. "Each company -- large, medium and small -- needs to pick its spots," he said.

But Wayne Allen, chairman of Phillips Petroleum Corp, said the oil companies that went through the painful restructuring in the late 1980s and early 1990s have learned their lesson on overpaying for assets and investing in non-petroleum ventures.
"I think it will be different this time around," he said. "None of us enjoyed downsizing and we're not sure that the prices and margins we enjoy today are here to stay."
